dataset.description: The complete publisher's historical Shanghai land-cover original in the fixed March 2023 East-of-China release. One full ZIP and its unchanged full single-band GeoTIFF are stored with independent byte/SHA receipts. This is an explicitly reviewed large tiled grid, not nationwide discovery, an RGB image, a clipped AOI export or an annual observation map.

layers.title: Shanghai land-cover classes · unchanged whole original
layers.valueInterpretation: Original UInt8 categorical codes, scale 1 and offset 0. Embedded scalar NoData is 0. Publisher legend: 1 Traffic route, 2 Tree cover, 3 Shrubland, 4 Grassland, 5 Cropland, 6 Building, 7 Barren and sparse vegetation, 8 Snow and ice, 9 Water, 10 Wetland, 12 Moss and lichen. Class 11 is not listed in the guide despite having an embedded green palette entry; 250 and 255 are not declared NoData or guide-defined fill codes. Their raw values and original palette are retained without inventing class meaning. This is a predicted classification, not quantitative reflectance or a calibrated land measurement.

dataset.version: East of China, March 2023 fixed original
warnings: This exact original is 132000 × 114000 (15048000000 grid pixels) in 230136 256 × 256 LZW tiles and has no overview. It exceeds ordinary axis/grid/chunk ceilings. Only the independently verified whole-member SHA and full physical profile may use the explicit reviewed large-grid policy; ordinary source limits remain unchanged.

Each original tile is at most 65536 decoded UInt8 bytes. Browsing chooses a lower-detail display within the unchanged 128 MiB per-chunk, 512 MiB cumulative preview and per-stage cooperative 30-second deadlines; no hard 30-second promise is made for a complete file hash/inspection. Full source bytes, original grid and full-resolution raw samples remain unchanged. A browsing PNG is not the full-resolution original.

The source mosaic was selected from the December 2021 Google Earth version, with actual source imagery captured across years. The publisher's separate 0.3-degree capture-time map gives Shanghai coarse-cell values including 2019, 2020 and 2021; it does not establish a common or per-pixel 1-m observation year. Publication in 2023 is not an observation date.
This fixed historical original retains its original edges and any overlap artefacts. The later author 2026 edge-fix script is not silently applied, and no new corrected original is fabricated.

The exact original ColorMap matches all eleven publisher class colors. Legend source: https://essd.copernicus.org/articles/15/4749/2023/essd-15-4749-2023-t02.png (SHA 9947f5aacde0e73336520fb5de39c5ecff07469831260bf8c546e98c00c2d5a9). The original TIFF photometric tag is BlackIsZero (1), separately from its ColorMap; map colors express categorical classes, not RGB sensor bands.

Author guide: https://zenodo.org/records/8214871. Timing evidence only: https://zenodo.org/records/8214467/files/Image_capture_time.tif (262584 bytes, SHA b233db58213971f8cc8eb6c77c8c249951235ab925772999fb16d0e70244b7ac, 0.3° grid). It is not selected as the land-cover product.

Only this exact SHA-256 and complete profile-reviewed SinoLC Shanghai original is admitted with its fixed 132000 × 114000 grid and 230136 indexed tiles. Ordinary axis, 8-billion-pixel and chunk ceilings remain unchanged. Reading uses individual 256 × 256 UInt8 tiles; no whole-grid array is allocated. The original grid and classification values are retained, with the existing 128 MiB per-chunk, 512 MiB cumulative preview and timeout limits.

The SinoLC preview maps unchanged class codes through this original's exact ColorMap. It displays categorical colors, not RGB sensor bands or a numerical grayscale calibration. Embedded NoData 0 is transparent; unlisted codes retain their original color without an invented class meaning.

This exact SHA-256 and profile-reviewed original has no embedded overview. Its display preview uses the largest pixel grid that fits the unchanged 512 MiB cumulative chunk budget. This low-detail class-color preview is for browsing only; original bytes, full-resolution raw pixel values, class codes and georeference are unchanged.
